articles.title: 5 popular streamers Ethan Klein has sued in the past 3 years: iDubbbz, Denims and more
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Ethan Klein's legal battles with streamers have taken a few unexpected turns since 2025. The latest name to enter the picture was iDubbbz, who faced a.
articles.body: Ethan Klein's legal battles with streamers have taken a few unexpected turns since 2025. The latest name to enter the picture was iDubbbz, who faced a defamation lawsuit that was filed separately from the copyright cases involving several Twitch streamers. The earlier lawsuits all traced back to Klein's 102-minute “Content Nuke: Hasan Piker” video. Four streamers eventually became defendants in that dispute, although their situations were far from identical. One settled, another received a default judgment, one is still fighting, and one got added to the case later.1. iDubbbzThe most recent lawsuit on the list involved Ian “iDubbbz” Jomha and had nothing to do with the earlier copyright dispute.In January 2026, Kick streamer Destiny made a sarcastic comment suggesting that Klein had molested his own children. Klein said he didn't sue Destiny because he understood that the remark wasn't serious.Jomha later displayed Destiny's comment for roughly 40 minutes while playing an alter-ego character, without adding much context. Klein subsequently filed a defamation lawsuit against Jomha in Calgary, Alberta. Jomha confirmed the case on June 9, saying, “It is official. I am being sued by Ethan Klein.”The case ended quickly. Jomha apologized and admitted that using Klein's children as “an attack vector” was wrong. Klein dropped the lawsuit the same day.2. SeanDaBlackSeanDaBlack, whose real name is Sean Wiggs, became part of Klein's copyright dispute after the original filing.He wasn't included when Klein and Hila, through their company Ted Entertainment, filed the lawsuit in June 2025. He was added later, becoming the fourth named defendant in the same case alongside Denims, Kaceytron and Frogan.There's considerably less publicly detailed information about SeanDaBlack's individual stream than there is about the other defendants. His case also received much less coverage.3. FroganFrogan's case took another route.The former Hasan Piker moderator reportedly left Klein's video running while she stepped away from her desk. When she came back, she asked, “What happened?”Klein's lawsuit also pointed to her sarcastic comment, “It's time to watch the new Nuke ethically,” as evidence that she knew what she was doing with the video.Her legal team then missed the deadline to respond. In May 2026, the court clerk entered a default against her. Klein later said on his podcast that Frogan's side had simply been misinformed about what was happening with the case.4. KaceytronKaceytron's stream stood out for a completely different reason.According to Klein's complaint, she smoked marijuana roughly 42 times while the broadcast was running and provided relatively little commentary. At some points, she admitted she didn't understand what she was watching.She also told viewers they could watch “without necessarily supporting Ethan Klein.”Unlike Denims, Kaceytron didn't continue the fight through the case. She settled with Klein in December 2025. The settlement reportedly involved a public apology as well as funds connected to her own fundraiser.5. DenimsAlexandra “Denims” Saber is the oldest case on this reverse-chronology list and the only one of the four original Content Nuke defendants still actively fighting.When Klein's video came out in February 2025, Denims streamed the entire 102-minute video. She paused it 211 times, using those breaks to comment on and challenge his claims.One line became especially relevant to Klein's lawsuit. Denims told viewers, “if you enjoyed not giving any views to that terrible video, follow, subscribe, throw a prime.” The lawsuit later used that statement as evidence she was deliberately trying to deny Klein revenue.Her legal defense has continued into 2026. Denims raised more than $58,000 toward a $100,000 GoFundMe goal for legal costs. A tentative ruling in June 2026 leaned toward finding her reaction protected under fair use, although the judge had not fully settled the issue.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UK lawmaker warns it’s ‘open season’ on Christians as he sounds alarm over ‘two-tier justice’
articles.summary: British lawmaker says it is 'open season' to discriminate against Christians in the United Kingdom while Islamist preachers go free.
articles.body: A British lawmaker is sounding the alarm over what he calls "two-tier justice" against Christians in the United Kingdom, telling Fox News Digital it is now "open season" to discriminate against believers while accusing authorities of allowing extremist Islamist preachers to operate as Christian pastors face harassment and arrest. Lord Jackson of Peterborough, vice chair of a parliamentary group focused on religious freedom, made the charge while discussing Finnish parliamentarian Päivi Räsänen, a Christian politician whose statements about marriage and sexuality have put her at the center of a years-long European battle over religious expression and free speech. "It does say a lot about the concerns that many of us have about attacks on Christians, and two-tier justice as between Christians and other faiths, and the fact that Christians, are, it's open season to discriminate against Christians in the United Kingdom now, and that's a very regrettable position," Jackson told Fox News Digital in an interview. CHRISTIAN SCHOOL CHAPLAIN WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER FIRING OVER LGBTQ SERMON Räsänen said British authorities canceled her electronic travel authorization, or ETA, in July before she applied for a visa, following her recent "hate speech" conviction over passages in a church booklet discussing homosexuality, raising fresh concerns among religious freedom advocates about the consequences of the ruling. According to ADF International, which has been representing Räsänen in litigation, Räsänen was granted a U.K. visa on Aug. 21, but not in time for her to speak in person about free speech at an event in Northern Ireland. "Räsänen was still blocked from speaking in person about free speech at an event in Northern Ireland yesterday, since she was granted her visa too late to attend," Alliance Defending Freedom International said in an Aug. 22 X post. "Räsänen was informed at 6.45pm last night that her visa application had been successful, and at 7.30pm she spoke remotely at the event, where she mentioned she was blocked from attending in person due to her ETA being cancelled in July." BIBLE VERSE LEADS TO TRIAL IN EUROPE. GROWING CRACKDOWN THREATENS OUR US-UK VALUES "We do not have the same free speech protections that are available to citizens of the United States," Jackson said. "And in this case, this particular lady expressed views, traditional views based on Scripture of her belief in a relationship in the eyes of God between a man and a woman, a relationship, that marriage between a man and a woman is central to societal stability, and that she was speaking what she had read in the Bible, and the fact was that activists have used her words and her sincere faith-based beliefs to attack her and to use lawfare to ensure that she is stigmatized and criminalized." Jackson, who has served in the House of Lords, the upper house of the Parliament of the United Kingdom, since November 2022, said he believes Muslims in the country are treated differently than Christians. "Extreme Islamist preachers being allowed to preach in parts of the United Kingdom whilst at the same time Christian pastors are being harassed and arrested on the street, that cannot stand, that's completely unacceptable," Jackson claimed. The British lawmaker said some of his peers are working to change direction and have greater protections of free speech. UK PASTOR SAYS HE WAS ARRESTED FOR PREACHING THE GOSPEL, SPEAKING OUT AGAINST ISLAM "We're fighting back in parliament and outside parliament," Jackson said. "We're working with various advocacy groups such as Christian Concern, the Christian Institute and others, and we're giving legal support to those people who are under attack. Women who, for instance, don't want to undress in a changing room with transgender women, i.e. men, women who are proud to wear a crucifix or a cross at work, and they are found to be committing a so-called microaggression." articles.title: Jive Bunny And The Mastermixers creator John Pickles dies at 84
articles.summary: Tributes are paid to John Pickles, who formed the novelty pop act in Rotherham in 1989.
articles.body:
The man behind the novelty pop act Jive Bunny and The Mastermixers has died aged 84, the company he founded has confirmed.

John Pickles formed Jive Bunny in Rotherham in 1989 and the act went on to have three UK number ones with Swing The Mood, That's What I Like and Let's Party.

Jive Bunny records typically used synthesisers and sampling to combine contemporary pop music with hits from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

A statement from the Mastermix company described Pickles as "a true pioneer in the music industry", adding that he was "a leader, an entrepreneur, a businessman and an incredibly talented songwriter".

His "creativity, vision and passion for music touched the lives and careers of so many people around the world, and for the most fortunate of us, he was dad," the statement said.

Jive Bunny And The Mastermixers were made up of Pickles, his son Andrew, who also worked as a director for Mastermix, along with Doncaster DJ and producer Les Hemstock.

The group also had a UK top 10 album in Jive Bunny The Album and scored five UK top 10 hits, including their number ones.

The Jive Bunny album covers and music videos featured a cartoon rabbit, with costumed actors also making promotional appearances as the character.

Steve White, a DJ who knew Pickles personally, told BBC Radio Sheffield the group's chart success had been "a people's success story".

"It was something that the family could enjoy," White said.

In December 2024, Mastermix released a new Jive Bunny production called 3, 6, 9.

It was said by the company to be "celebrating the origins of Jive Bunny while adding a modern twist".

articles.title: AIX crew member under scanner after handwriting probe
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Matching handwriting on a threat note found in the lav of a diverted Air India Express international flight with that of all 40 people on b.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Matching handwriting on a threat note found in the lav of a diverted Air India Express international flight with that of all 40 people on board has reportedly brought a crew member under the scanner of investigating agencies.A passenger's role is also being probed. This Monday's Dammam-Delhi flight (IX 170) was diverted to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words "bomb red 430" written on it and a box, both in black ink, drawn on it was found in the lav.On landing in Ahmedabad, AI Express filed a complaint with the airport police, seeking a probe into who might have written the threat note. So apart from the normal protocol of checking passengers, aircraft and baggage, handwriting tests on all the 32 passengers, four cabin crew members and four pilots (airlines send extra crew to areas impacted by the US-Iran war to handle last-minute diversions)."The agencies had asked the airline to give the same tissue paper for getting handwriting samples. Six tissues were sought for each passenger," said sources. AI Express arranged an alternate aircraft with new set of crew members that flew all the 32 passengers to Delhi on Monday-Tuesday midnight.The crew members were asked to stay back for the probe. It is learnt that of them, seven were told Thursday they were free to leave the city. "The role of a crew member is being examined apart from a passenger also being under the scanner," said sources. To be sure, no one has been conclusively found to have written the threat note and the probe is on.An Air India Express spokesperson said: "We are aware that law enforcement agencies are investigating a security-related incident involving our flight operating from Dammam to Delhi on Aug 31, pursuant to a complaint filed by us. The airline is fully cooperating with the relevant agencies in the investigation. We unequivocally condemn any conduct that compromises or has the potential to compromise the safety and security of our guests, crew and operations. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Seattle police union sounds alarm after city axes officer hiring bonuses amid staffing shortage
articles.summary: Seattle's police union warns the city's decision to cut up to $50,000 in hiring bonuses could worsen a staffing crisis with only 927 deployable officers.
articles.body: Seattle's police union is sounding the alarm after the city eliminated lucrative hiring bonuses for new and experienced officers despite the department remaining hundreds of cops short, warning the move could make it even harder to compete with neighboring departments for recruits. "Public safety should be the cornerstone of every city budget," Seattle Police Officers Guild President Kent Loux told Fox News Digital after the city ended incentives that had offered $7,500 to new recruits and as much as $50,000 to experienced officers willing to join the Seattle Police Department. "Unfortunately, Mayor Katie has proven time and again that public safety is not a priority, but rather an inconvenience to be addressed after tragedy strikes. AS SOCIALIST MAYOR BATTLES ICE, SEATTLE POLICE AND CRIME VICTIMS SAY REPEAT OFFENDERS ARE TERRORIZING THE CITY "The decision to eliminate hiring incentives is baffling. Seattle has still not recovered from the consequences of the defund-the-police movement that began in 2020, and we remain hundreds of officers short. Now is the time to be aggressively recruiting qualified officers, not eliminating one of the tools that helps us compete for them. If this is the direction the mayor intends to take, the future of public safety in Seattle does not look positive." Fox 13 Seattle reported Wednesday that the city stopped its hiring incentives for police recruits, slashing bonuses that provided as much as $50,000 for lateral officers joining from other law enforcement agencies. Local outlet Kiro 7 reported that entry-level hires would qualify for $7,500, plus up to $5,000 in moving expenses if the move exceeds 50 miles, while lateral hires or officers that move from another department can receive up to $50,000 and $7,500 for relocation. KOMO News recently reported that the Seattle Police Department is "hundreds of officers short of its staffing goals, with only 927 deployable officers," with some outlets reporting that the department is short at least 300 officers from full staffing. SEATTLE MAYOR GRILLED ON PUBLIC SAFETY CRISIS AS RESIDENTS DEMAND ANSWERS The outlet noted that the Bellevue Police Department posted on Aug. 28 on X that officers joining its department from another department would get a $30,000 signing bonus in addition to other incentives. "A decision has been made to stop the hiring incentives until a time when the budget forecast for the Seattle Police Department is clear," the Seattle Police Department said in a statement shared with Fox 13. SEATTLE POLICE CHIEF SNAPS OVER CHICAGO HOME QUESTIONS, ABSENCE FROM CITY AFTER MASS SHOOTING The department added, "We have a responsibility to the people of Seattle to provide the best police service while also being fiscally responsible. We will continue to hire some of the highest quality candidates in the country and are dedicated to helping keep Seattle a safe and welcoming city." In a statement provided to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the office of Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said, "Seattle police officers play a critical role in keeping our communities safe, and Mayor Wilson values their service. The decision to adjust incentive pay was not made lightly. It reflects the fiscal realities facing our city and the need to align compensation with long-term sustainability across all departments. "Having said that, for the first time since 2019, we're seeing fewer officers leave the department, and SPD hired almost 100 officers over the past eight months. There are also 3,500 applications under review. Over the next few months, Interim Chief Sayles is focusing on operations and working to unlock the bottleneck of getting new officers thoughtfully through training and on the street." articles.title: In 1906, five railroad bridges carried coal through West Virginia’s New River Gorge; 120 years later an $11.8 million project is rebuilding them for hikers
articles.summary: US News: Five railroad bridges built in 1906 to carry coal through West Virginia’s New River Gorge are getting a new purpose more than a century later. An $11..
articles.body: Five railroad bridges built in 1906 to carry coal through West Virginia’s New River Gorge are getting a new purpose more than a century later. An $11.8 million restoration project is now under way to repair the bridges and reopen the historic trail for visitors.According to the National Park Service (NPS), the project began on September 1, 2026, with a ceremonial groundbreaking at the Minden Trailhead. The project is being funded through the Great American Outdoors Act Legacy Restoration Fund. The National Park Foundation and Friends of New River Gorge joined the NPS for the event.The restoration is focused on the Rend Trail, formerly known as the Thurmond-Minden Trail. The 3.2-mile trail runs along the New River and Dunloup Creek and provides views of the historic downtown and community of Thurmond.Five bridges built for coal trainsThe Rend Trail follows an old railroad grade that was built in 1906 to haul coal. Today, the same route is used as a recreational trail and crosses five historic railroad trestles, or bridges.However, more than 100 years of exposure and use have left the wooden structures in poor condition. According to the NPS, structural risks caused by the ageing infrastructure have resulted in partial closures along the trail. One of the main bridges has been closed for several years because it became too unsafe for people to cross.The restoration will remove the existing wooden bridges and replace them with durable aluminium tread, according to Acting Superintendent Eric LaPrice.The project is not limited to the bridges. The NPS said it will also repair key retaining walls and resurface the trail. The path will also be rerouted around Big Rock, where the existing terrain has made access difficult.Trail to be accessible againAnother major part of the work will focus on making the trail easier to access. The project will regrade the trail, improve drainage and add a restroom at the trailhead.The stairs at Big Rock will also be replaced with an accessible ramp. This is expected to help open the full trail to people of all abilities.The work is intended to restore the Rend Trail as a continuous route. At present, partial closures mean visitors cannot travel through the entire trail.“The trail was partially closed, so it wasn’t a through trail. Now, when this work is done, it’s going to be a through trail again. It’s going to connect to another area of the park and it’s going to connect to the trails that the community has here. So it’s a connection to the community," LaPrice said.The Thurmond and Minden/Oak Hill trailheads will also be rehabilitated as part of the project. Together, the improvements are intended to address safety problems and reconnect the trail with nearby communities. 16 months to goThe NPS expects the construction work to take about 16 months. The agency hopes to reopen the complete trail with a ribbon-cutting ceremony next fall.The restoration is also expected to support tourism in the surrounding area. The NPS said spending by visitors to the park generated an estimated $95.5 million for the local economy in 2024.The project is being paid for through the Legacy Restoration Fund, which was created under the Great American Outdoors Act. The fund expired in September 2025, and supporters are now seeking its renewal.Paul Coussan, vice president of government relations for the National Park Foundation, said efforts are under way to extend the programme.“We have a lot of support in Congress right now on the America the Beautiful Act, which would take this great program that was created back in 2020, the Legacy Restoration Fund, and extend it for another five years,” Coussan said. “So we’re really working to get that done.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Peace hinges on diplomacy, not oil trade: EAM in Ukraine
articles.summary: India News: The Russia-Ukraine conflict will be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and not by dwelling over who is buying oil from where, said external affai.
articles.body: The Russia-Ukraine conflict will be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and not by dwelling over who is buying oil from where, said external affairs minister S Jaishankar rejecting the Western narrative that countries buying energy from Russia are bankrolling President Vladimir Putin's war.Reiterating India's stance, the minister stressed that while the responsibility of ending the conflict rested with the parties involved, New Delhi stood ready to extend any necessary assistance to facilitate peace. Jaishankar was speaking alongside his Ukraine counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv after a meeting in which he recalled PM Narendra Modi's message to Putin last week that the endless war must now give way to end of war. The minister also called on President Volodymyr Zelensky later to discuss "approaches to end the ongoing conflict".Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure adequate, affordable and reliable supplies came in response to a question if India would consider cutting down purchase of Russian oil because of US sanctions."It's important that you get the challenges of providing energy for 1.4 billion people at a time when the world energy situation is very difficult. Ukraine has its perspective, which we respect. And we have ours, which I would expect others to also respect," said the minister. "This conflict, which is today in its fifth year, will not be solved because somebody is buying or not buying oil or minerals or fertilisers. This conflict will be solved by dialogue, by diplomacy, by negotiations ... and that's why it is something we would encourage."Zelensky later said that even while Jaishankar was in Ukraine, Russia launched jet-powered Shahed drones that were developed not without Iran's help. Zelensky also thanked India for its commitment to ending "this unjust war - Russia's war against Ukraine". He added, "This certainly must not be a time of war. Peace is needed. This is India's clear position."This was Jaishankar's first visit to Ukraine since he accompanied Modi for his landmark trip to Kyiv, months after his visit to Moscow. Asked if India was looking forward to hosting Zelensky, the EAM did not confirm if he was going to extend an invitation to him. He invited Sybiha to visit India, though. Jaishankar reiterated Modi's message that each passing day of conflict only means more deaths and more destruction. "Understandably, it is for the parties involved to find a way. But, if India can be of any help in any manner, we are ready, and this was the core of my discussion so far with Sybiha," he said.Among other related issues raised were attacks on commercial shipping, with Jaishankar underlining that Indian seafarers man ships of many flags and have been among the casualties. "The impact on shipping is also significantly affecting many nations of the Global South," he said.In his remarks, Sybiha briefed Jaishankar about the "escalation from Russia and systemic Russian attacks on civilian ships, ports and infrastructure" and expressed condolences for the loss of Indian lives.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian-origin father and son's hotel empire in US accused of $100 million loan fraud and ponzi-like scheme
articles.summary: US News: An Indian-origin family running a hotel business in the US secured more than $100 million in loans over nearly three decades despite a history of loan.
articles.body: An Indian-origin family running a hotel business in the US secured more than $100 million in loans over nearly three decades despite a history of loan defaults, bankruptcies and court judgments, according to a civil complaint filed by the US Department of Justice. The allegations targeted hotel operators Pankaj Sheth and Rajan Sheth, five other relatives, 21 businesses and eight associates. The 332-page complaint alleged that the family used a network of companies and so-called “straw owners” to conceal their control of hotels and obtain fresh financing even after earlier loans had gone into default.According to the DOJ, the Sheths and their associates repeatedly shifted ownership or control of distressed hotel properties among different entities. Prosecutors alleged that the arrangement enabled companies linked to the family to apply for new loans without fully disclosing their relationships with earlier borrowers.The complaint alleged that some of the new financing was then used to repay older debts, allowing the businesses to continue operating and borrow additional money despite their previous financial problems.Who are the Sheths?The Sheths, who share a home in Morganville, presented themselves as a legitimate, family-owned hotel operator, a report by NJ.com said. But the business existed to keep loans flowing against properties that were falling apart — hotels that were “chronically understaffed, underfunded, and many were in gross disrepair,” drawing “public nuisance and accessibility complaints,” code violations and liens, according to the complaint.“DO NOT stay here,” one user wrote on Yelp reviewing one of their hotels. “Worst hotel I have ever been to. I used a whole can of Lysol to decontaminate…”Rajan Sheth has publicly denied the allegations, saying the business is legitimate. “My clients deny they are liable to the United States for the claims that have been filed and look forward to being vindicated at trial,” Richard Scheff, an attorney for the family, said in a statement to NJ.com.What are the allegationsThe Sheths would borrow against a hotel, use the money to pay off an older debt, then borrow again to cover the new one. The Sheths hid their financial history and every time they needed a loan, they’d put a hotel in the name of a “straw owner” — someone whose name is on the paperwork but who has no real control — according to the complaint. Then that “straw owner” would apply for the loan. The applications often “falsified the straw owners’ management experience and personal financial statements,” concealed the company’s ties to the rest of the family’s troubled businesses and sometimes even forged signatures, prosecutors allege.The family “haphazardly manipulated membership interests according to their needs at any given time, leaving a confusing, and often contradictory, trail of corporate organizational and tax records in their wake,” according to the complaint.Once a loan came through, the Sheths diverted the money to pay off an older debt to a different lender that was threatening foreclosure. Then that new loan would go bad too, and the family would go looking for the next one.If they couldn’t get a new loan, the family had one last move -- filing for bankruptcy at the last moment.“The Sheths repeated this cycle many times,” prosecutors alleged.Sheths sold a New Jersey hotel to themselvesA hotel in Browns Mills was on sale. It was later found that the buyer was a company that belonged to the Sheths only. The family had sold the hotel to itself — and gotten a federal judge to erase most of a taxpayer-backed debt.The lawsuit is civil, not criminal, so no one faces prison time, the report said. But the financial stakes are high: across 133 counts under the False Claims Act and a federal banking-fraud law, prosecutors are asking a judge to order the Sheths to repay what the government lost, triple those damages, and pay a penalty of up to $11,000 for each false claim. They also want the family to return every dollar it pocketed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IShowSpeed devastated after hearing about Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football
articles.summary: US Streamers News: IShowSpeed looked completely stunned when he found out Lionel Messi had officially called time on his Argentina international career. The streamer was.
articles.body: IShowSpeed looked completely stunned when he found out Lionel Messi had officially called time on his Argentina international career. The streamer was watching Fabrizio Romano’s announcement during a livestream when the news appeared on his screen. What followed was less of a normal reaction and more of Speed trying to convince himself that the post couldn’t be real. The 39-year-old Messi announced his decision on August 31, 2026, after an Argentina campaign that ended with a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. He leaves international football with 207 appearances and a record 125 goals for his country. For Speed, though, the numbers almost seemed beside the point.Speed could not believe Romano’s announcementA clip shared by the IShowSpeedHQ X account shows the streamer sitting at his desk in headphones and a black “Humble” T-shirt. He stares at Romano’s post, looking increasingly shocked as he processes what he is reading.Then came the plea.“Fabrizio Romano, tell me you’re lying right now… I know you don’t lie. I know Fabrizio Romano does NOT lie,” Speed said.That reaction captures just how difficult the announcement was for him to accept. He reportedly also argued that Messi still has the ability to play and “should NOT retire.”Speed is famously associated with Cristiano Ronaldo, but his reactions to Messi have still produced some memorable football moments. During the 2026 World Cup, he had already shown mixed emotions around Messi, including empathy after seeing the Argentine star cry in the final.Why Messi decided to step awayMessi’s own explanation adds a much heavier layer to the announcement. He said the decision was made two days after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat. The death of his father, Jorge, in early August then left him “even more convinced” that retirement was the right choice.In his statement, Messi described the decision as something that “hurt, and still hurts, deep in my soul.” After years of giving everything to Argentina, he said he had “nothing left to give.”He also praised the younger generation coming through and thanked the supporters and his family. Messi made clear that stepping away does not mean walking away from Argentina completely. He said he will continue supporting the national team from the sidelines.For now, the retirement only applies to his international career. Messi is still playing club football for Inter Miami.That distinction, however, did little to soften Speed’s reaction. Watching the announcement land in real time, the streamer seemed to be dealing with the end of an era rather than just one football retirement.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Three farmers detained by Israel in Lebanon, village leader says
articles.summary: The detentions were reported to the US-led International Monitoring and Implementation Mechanism but Israeli military has not commented.
articles.body:
Three Lebanese farmers have been detained by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, according to the leader of their village.

Issa Abedelaal told the BBC that Israeli forces called the three farmers on their mobile phones and instructed them to report to a location, where they were detained and taken away.

It came after Israeli forces had entered the village of Halta in Hasbaya province, which lies within a roughly 600 sq km area that Israel continues to occupy.

The detentions were reported to the US-led International Monitoring and Implementation Mechanism, which oversees security coordination between Israel and Lebanon. The Israeli military has not replied to a request for comment.

Hours later, Israel released another Lebanese civilian held in the country, in what is believed to be the first known civilian release since US-mediated talks between Israel and Lebanon began in April.

Malek Ghazi was handed over to the Lebanese army by the International Committee of the Red Cross, while Israel says four more Lebanese civilians will be released on Friday.

More than 30 Lebanese are still believed to be in Israeli custody, as negotiations between the two countries remain stalled over a framework involving Hezbollah's disarmament, an Israeli withdrawal and the deployment of the Lebanese army in the south.

Ghazi was handed over at the Naqoura crossing before being taken to an army intelligence facility in Tyre for a medical examination.

His family says he disappeared last October after leaving home to exercise.

Israel's prime minister's office said four other civilians due to be released on Friday had been questioned and found to have no links to armed groups.

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam welcomed Ghazi's release and thanked the US for its role in securing it.

He said the government would continue working for the release of all Lebanese detainees, information about those still missing, and a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

The detainee issue is part of wider US-mediated negotiations, alongside separate efforts to recover the remains of Lebanese Jewish community leaders abducted and killed during the country's civil war.

The negotiations also cover a framework agreed in mid-June, under which Hezbollah is expected to disarm, the Lebanese army to deploy in the south and Israeli forces to withdraw gradually, beginning with designated "pilot zones".

But the process has made little headway, with Israel questioning the role of the Lebanese army and disagreements over how compliance would be verified.

Hezbollah rejects the talks and the pilot-zone concept outright.

The two sides have yet to set a date for the eighth round of talks.

Israel has continued attacks on southern Lebanon, and officials say the Israeli military has been expanding its positions .

Lebanese authorities said 11 people were killed in an Israeli air strike on the region in August. Israel's Defense Forces (IDF) said at the time that it had killed a Hezbollah commander in the strike, following an attack against Israeli soldiers.

articles.title: Meet Jiya Patel, the 17-year-old from Columbus, Georgia who turned restaurant leftovers into a 40-chapter network donating over $100,000 worth of food
articles.summary: US News: At just 17, Jiya Patel is already making an impact far beyond her school in Columbus, Georgia. A rising senior, Jiya balances academics with the schoo.
articles.body: At just 17, Jiya Patel is already making an impact far beyond her school in Columbus, Georgia. A rising senior, Jiya balances academics with the school golf team, Honor Council and Student Live Committee, where she helps organise events such as prom and pep rallies. But her biggest contribution extends beyond the school campus.According to Points of Light, Jiya is the co-founder of Thrive2Gethr, a student-led initiative that tackles two major issues at once: food waste and food insecurity. What began as a personal response to something she witnessed during a family trip to India has now grown into a nationwide network with around 1,200 members across 40 student-led chapters.Together, the chapters have facilitated donations of more than $100,000 worth of food from restaurants and bakeries to shelters and food banks.A trip to India sparked an ideaJiya’s interest in volunteering began at her local temple, where she helped serve food and took part in gardening, cleaning and other activities. But a visit to India with her parents in 2023 changed the way she thought about hunger.“I went to India with my parents and saw a lot of families without food and necessary resources. It stuck with me, and I started thinking a lot about hunger,” Jiya said.She soon began looking into food waste in the United States and came across videos showing perfectly edible food being discarded.“I realized that food waste and people facing food insecurity could be connected to address both problems. The food already existed; it just wasn’t getting to people who needed it,” she explained.That realisation led Jiya to co-found Thrive2Gethr in 2023.From hearing ‘no’ to building 40 chaptersGetting the initiative off the ground was far from easy. In the early days, Jiya personally approached restaurants and other businesses in her community, hoping to convince them to donate excess food.“I would make a list of 100 businesses and struggle to find any partners. Many would just say no, right off the bat,” she recalled.But rejection did not stop her.“I’d keep following up with the ones that were leaning towards maybe,” she said.Jiya also coordinated volunteers who collected the food and delivered it to shelters. As the organisation expanded, her role evolved from making local connections to mentoring other young leaders.Today, she recruits and supports student chapter leaders, helps them establish relationships with restaurants, creates guides and resources, and answers questions as they build their own programmes.She estimates that she spends around 30 hours each month volunteering.Building a movement led by young peopleFor Jiya, the goal is not simply to make Thrive2Gethr bigger. She wants to ensure that existing chapters receive the support they need while continuing to expand.“I want to keep expanding, but I want to ensure each of our chapters is still getting the support they need,” she said, stressing the importance of finding a balance between growth and maintaining the organisation’s existing network.Another priority is encouraging restaurants to become more comfortable with food donations. Jiya believes concerns about potential liability can sometimes discourage businesses from participating.She points to the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act of 1996, a federal law that provides certain protections for people who donate food in good faith.Thrive2Gethr provides restaurants with information about the law as part of its outreach, while also trying to raise awareness about food donation more broadly.The reward goes beyond the foodThe impact of the initiative, Jiya says, is not measured only in the amount of food redistributed. She also finds meaning in seeing other students become involved in helping their communities.“Giving so much food to people who need it has been rewarding to see,” she said.Depending on the location, the food is either delivered to a facility for distribution or given directly to people in need.Jiya particularly enjoys watching student volunteers become invested in the work.“I’ve also enjoyed watching students help people in their communities and be invested in it the same way I am,” she said.What volunteering has taught herThrough the experience, Jiya has learned that creating change does not have to be a solo effort.“It’s a lot easier to make change when you work together,” she said, pointing to the partnerships between students, restaurants and shelters.The experience has also taught her persistence. Convincing businesses to participate often means hearing “no” repeatedly before finding someone willing to help.“You have to push forward and hope that someone will end up saying yes,” she said. “I don’t let things stop me when it gets hard.”‘You don’t have to be a full-grown adult to start making change’Jiya believes one of the biggest misconceptions about volunteering is that people need extensive experience or resources before they can make a difference.“Everyone has to do their part to help. If you’re able to, you should at least try. It doesn’t have to be big,” she said.Her own story, she believes, is proof that one person’s decision to act can eventually create a much larger movement.“If you care about something and you work at it, even something small can create a big ripple effect. You never know who you’ll inspire,” she added.Jiya encourages others to start by contacting local restaurants, getting involved with existing initiatives or even creating a Thrive2Gethr chapter in their community.Her advice is simple: start small and keep going.“You don’t have to be a full-grown adult to start making change,” she said. “If you care about something, just start, and everything will work itself out.”As she prepares to head to college and pursue a career in business or economics, Jiya is already leaving behind a framework that other young leaders can use to make a difference.For her, the hardest part is not building a nationwide network. It is simply taking that first step.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2002, Idaho buried nearly 300 tons of crushed waste glass beneath Highway 75; the material formed 8 to 12 inches of fill under a 200-foot road section
articles.summary: US News: Transport authorities in Idaho turned nearly 300 tonnes of discarded glass into road foundation material under Highway 75, creating a durable structur.
articles.body: Transport authorities in Idaho turned nearly 300 tonnes of discarded glass into road foundation material under Highway 75, creating a durable structural base while solving a local landfill crisis. The engineering trial, executed along a 200-foot stretch of highway near Ketchum, placed an eight-to-12-inch layer of crushed glass cullet directly beneath the road surface. Conceived by late Idaho State Senator Clint Stennett, the initiative redirected massive piles of glass accumulating at the Ohio Gulch Recycling Center in the Wood River Valley into practical civil infrastructure. "This project is an excellent example of Idahoans, business and government working together to use our resources in the best possible way," Stennett said during an Earth Day site visit alongside transport officials, as reported by industry journal Roads & Bridges. "It is critical that not only in highway projects, but in all aspects of our lives and businesses we look to reuse and recycle our critical resources."Engineering performance of glass culletInstead of letting discarded bottles collect in regional landfills, civil engineers crushed the material into small, granular fragments known as glass cullet. When crushed down to optimum particle sizes, glass behaves similarly to natural sand and crushed rock, exhibiting strong compaction and drainage characteristics. According to technical specifications published by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) in its User Guidelines for Waste and Byproduct Materials in Pavement Construction, glass cullet serves as an effective substitute for conventional aggregate in road embankments and base courses. The FHWA technical documentation notes that clean cullet displays high internal friction angles, good permeability, and low moisture susceptibility, making it stable under heavy traffic loads. When used as granular subbase or structural fill, crushed glass reduces thermal conductivity compared to natural stone. In cold climates like central Idaho, this thermal performance helps protect underlying road beds from severe freeze-thaw cycles, which frequently cause cracking and potholes in traditional asphalt surfaces.Overcoming local recycling bottlenecksThe Highway 75 pilot project addressed a widespread economic issue facing rural communities across the United States: the high cost of transporting post-consumer glass to distant processing plants. Because raw glass is heavy and yields low market value, municipal recycling programs in isolated areas often struggle to cover shipping costs to urban recycling centers. By processing waste glass locally and using it in nearby civil engineering projects, local authorities eliminated long-distance haulage fees while reducing the need to quarry virgin stone aggregates. Prior to the Idaho installation, laboratory evaluations guided by FHWA frameworks verified that properly crushed cullet poses minimal environmental or safety risks. When ground down to maximum particle sizes below 9.5 millimetres (3/8 inch), sharp edges are eliminated, allowing highway crews to handle the material using standard heavy construction equipment. Environmental testing further confirmed that inert glass does not leach harmful contaminants into surrounding groundwater or soil.Broader adoption in road infrastructureThe Idaho transport experiment built upon broader federal research evaluating industrial byproducts for highway construction. Federal guidelines highlight that incorporating processed cullet into subgrade layers, asphalt mixtures, and utility trench backfills offers double environmental savings by preserving natural aggregate reserves while extending landfill capacities. Highway agencies across several US states have since adopted guidelines allowing up to 10 to 15 per cent crushed glass content in asphalt wearing courses, and up to 30 per cent or higher in unbound subbase layers. The Highway 75 section demonstrated that processed municipal waste can meet strict engineering standards for load-bearing road foundations, providing transportation departments with a practical strategy for sustainable infrastructure development.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: British army told to stop non-essential training exercises to save money
articles.summary: Units in the UK not preparing to be deployed have been told to cut back on training exercises due to cost pressures.
articles.body:
The Army has been told to stop "non-essential" training exercises to save money, according to a defence source.

It will continue to train soldiers preparing to be deployed or on deployments - such as units sent to Estonia, the Falklands or Cyprus.

But units back in the UK and who are not preparing for a specific deployment have been told to cut back on collective training exercises due to financial pressures.

It comes as Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces pressure to increase spending on defence.

The government is increasing defence spending to 2.5% of national income by next year, but is under growing pressure to reach a target of 3% by the end of the decade.

A defence source said the plans mean not doing what he called "nice to have training" - like large live fire exercises and rehearsing platoon attacks in UK training areas like Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire and Sennybridge in Wales.

It is understood planned exercises that were due to take place that are now cancelled include one involving the Royal Tank Regiment conducting live fire drills in Wales and a separate exercise involving tanks and Apace helicopters.

This was not the choice of the army, the source said. The pause is expected to continue for most of this year.

Other specific training aimed at modernising the Army – such as practising drone and counter-drone warfare is expected to continue.

The Army says it is prioritising the training that has been informed by lessons learnt from the war in Ukraine, and is reviewing each request for training on a case-by-case basis.

Though the government is increasing defence spending, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) is still struggling to fund all its investment plans.

Much of the new money has been earmarked for specific capital projects, including new weapons programmes. The part of the MoD's budget for training is still under significant pressure.

An Army spokesperson said: "Our training continues and we are prioritising activity that contributes most directly to readiness, deployability and operational effectiveness.

"We are also investing £2bn to transform training for the British Army over the next 15 years."

On Wednesday during Prime Minister's Questions, the chairman of the Commons Defence Select Committee, Labour's Tan Singh Dhesi, warned it was imperative to invest in the armed forces and urged Burnham to commit to reaching 3% of GDP spend on defence by 2030.

The prime minister replied: "I've made that commitment very clear, and I have done for a considerable period of time."

The government's wavering over defence spending was part of the downfall of Burnham's predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer - with former Defence Secretary John Healey resigning his position in response to Sir Keir's plans on funding the armed forces.

Plans set out in the Defence Investment Plan (Dip) will see defence spending rise to 2.7% of GDP by 2027/28, but there are no firm details on how further increases will be achieved beyond that date.

The Treasury has consistently said the government will set out plans for reaching both 3% and 3.5% at the spending review, due to take place next year.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has urged the prime minister to "cut welfare spending and invest that money in our defence". The party says it would spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.

"Faced with a choice between spending on military training and spending on benefits... Labour chooses more benefits," Tory shadow secretary of state for work and pensions Helen Whately said.

articles.title: Meet Nithya Ravuri, the California high-school student whose nonprofit has grown to more than 500 members across 15 chapters while supporting neurodivergent children and families
articles.summary: US News: A student-led movement supporting neurodivergent children and their families has grown into a global network across several continents, led by a high .
articles.body: A student-led movement supporting neurodivergent children and their families has grown into a global network across several continents, led by a high school senior in California. Nithya Ravuri, a student at Emerald High School in Dublin, California, founded Sevah Neuro to provide accessible resources, social connections, and community support for children with neurological differences. What started as a local effort to create learning materials has grown into an organisation with more than 500 members and 15 chapters worldwide. The initiative began after Ravuri shadowed occupational and paediatric therapists and worked directly with children diagnosed with conditions including autism and Down syndrome. During this clinical experience, parents often told her about the lack of affordable specialised learning materials and the social isolation their children faced. Instead of accepting the lack of support, Ravuri started creating custom educational tools to help fill the gap. The project soon became a structured non-profit called Sevah Neuro, a name taken from the Sanskrit word for selfless service.Global expansion and chapter networkWorking with fellow Emerald High School student Aatmika Kapoor, who serves as chief operating officer, Ravuri strengthened the organisation and expanded the non-profit far beyond Northern California. According to reporting by The Independent and republished by SFGate, Sevah Neuro has established more than 15 chapters across the United States and other countries, including India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, Ghana, and Mexico. To provide direct support, the non-profit launched the Sevah Pediatric Neuroinclusion Fellowship, a five-week online summer programme offering life-skills lessons and organised social activities for more than 400 neurodivergent children. "We try providing them a safe space for them to grow as people and we teach them life skills," Ravuri said in an interview with local media outlet Livermore Vine. "I always wanted to start addressing this; giving them a safe space is one of my biggest priorities. But also, so other people, not just me, can learn from these children and see how talented they are."Overcoming operational challengesRunning a multi-chapter non-profit while attending high school brought administrative and personal challenges. In an interview with Bold Journey Magazine, Ravuri explained how early setbacks and self-doubt tested her commitment to the cause. "There were moments of real self-doubt, wondering if a 17-year-old could actually be taken seriously running an organization, balancing schoolwork with the responsibility of leading a team, and facing setbacks when partnerships fell through or plans didn't work the way I expected," Ravuri said. To keep the organisation moving forward, the leadership team focused on building steady and sustainable working habits instead of chasing short-term attention. "Consistency: SEVAH Neuro didn't grow from one big moment; it grew from continuing to show up for the kids and their families, even after the initial excitement wore off," Ravuri told Bold Journey Magazine.Legislative advocacy and future developmentAlong with family support and educational programmes, Sevah Neuro has expanded into policy advocacy. The student organisation has lobbied California state officials for greater public awareness and more educational resources about neurodivergence, with plans to take its advocacy to federal lawmakers. The organisation is also developing an educational book and a dedicated mobile app to give parents and caregivers direct access to learning tools. Looking ahead, Ravuri hopes Sevah Neuro will become a permanent institution that can open specialised trusts and physical educational centres. "When people hear Sevah, they should always think about the work we've done and the children we impacted rather than the people behind it," Ravuri told The Independent. "And not just me, we have a huge team."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Feds charge ICE officer with lying to investigators in the shooting of Venezuelan immigrant
articles.summary: A federal grand jury returned an indictment against Christian Castro in the January shooting that left Julio Cesar Sosa Celis with a gunshot wound in one of his legs.
articles.body: An ICE officer is facing federal charges for allegedly lying to federal investigators about the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant during immigration enforcement operations in Minneapolis earlier this year. A federal grand jury on Wednesday returned an indictment charging the officer, Christian Castro, with making false statements to the FBI about the Jan. 14 shooting that left Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis with a gunshot wound in his leg, a source familiar with the investigation told NBC News. A separate investigation into whether Castro should face a more serious civil rights charge in the shooting is ongoing, the source added. The Associated Press first reported on Castro’s latest federal charges. The federal charges come a week after Castro was released from jail in Texas despite an extradition warrant from Minnesota prosecutors seeking his transfer. He’s facing state charges in Minnesota accusing him of assault and false reporting of a crime related to the same shooting. Federal authorities had initially accused Sosa-Celis and another man of beating an immigration officer with a broom handle and a snow shovel in a confrontation that preceded the shooting, but federal prosecutors dropped the charges they filed against the men after video evidence showed the ICE officers may have lied about the encounter. Castro was arrested in May in the Minnesota case. He was held in custody in Brownsville, Texas, until his release last week after a judge and Gov. Greg Abbott refused to sign his extradition warrant — citing fraud investigations involving social services programs in Minnesota, which the Trump administration used to justify his immigration crackdown there. Andrew Mahaleris, Abbott’s press secretary, told NBC News that “state law enforcement stands ready and willing to assist federal partners in facilitating Mr. Castro’s arrest if needed.” Mahaleris added that “details of any federal indictment are best addressed to the U.S. Department of Justice.” The Department of Homeland Security and the Minnesota Attorney General’s Office referred any queries to the DOJ. An attorney for Castro did not immediately respond to a request for comment. As news broke of Castro’s latest indictment, a federal prosecutor working on the case against Castro was fired, two sources familiar with the matter told NBC News. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Evans had told lawyers for Sosa-Celis that DOJ officials have blocked efforts to bring the more serious civil rights charge against Castro, ProPublica reported on Wednesday. Evans did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and his DOJ email address returned an automated reply saying he was on leave.

articles.title: Poverty, inequality seed delinquency in minors: SC
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent be.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour due to having grown up in poverty and environs marked by inequality, illiteracy and discrimination, Supreme Court has said.Exonerating a minor from the charge of attempt to erase evidence in a dowry death case, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sh-ree Chandrashekhar traced in detail the history and development of JJ Act. They said because of industrialisation and urbanisation, rural folk migrated to cities and this weakened community cohesion, resulting in families losing control over their children.Writing the judgement, Justice Chandrashekhar said Wednesday, "Poverty, inequality, illiteracy and the discriminatory environment in which a child grows trigger delinquent behaviour... The rise in the number of cases coming to this court raising the plea of juvenility for the first time indicates in ample measure that there is a huge gap in understanding of the law by stakeholders."The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar' where they held "today's children are exposed to complex information, graphic content and adult experience that were inaccessible to the previous generation".Writing the July 21 judgement, Justice Pardiwala had analysed what propelled a person to commit a crime - "It could be enmity, it could be poverty, it could be greed, it could be perversity in mind and many others..." But the bench had not mentioned inequality, illiteracy, or a discriminatory environment as grounds for a child to turn delinquent.The bench had further said, "There is no doubt that proliferation of technology and the pervasive influence of social media has altered the cognitive and psychological development of children. In such circumstances, courts as living institutions must be responsive to this reality.""The approach of courts or the juvenile justice boards dealing with a child in conflict with the law cannot remain stagnant since the legislation came to be enacted. It must bear a balanced approach towards the evolving nature of the juvenile and legitimate demands of society," Justices Pardiwala and Bhuyan had further said.Justices Mishra and Chandrashekhar said the prosecution's eagerness to bring the culprit to court and forgetting to assess the boy's age led to overlooking of JJ Act and violation of the rights of juveniles in conflict with the law."A child should not be treated as a criminal. He is a victim of the circumstances. Sometimes he is drawn to a world of crime due to socio-economic or emotional and psychological reasons. The state owes a responsibility to reintegrate juveniles in society, rather than permanently stigmatising them," Justice Chandrashekhar said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Natalie Harp came in, gave Trump a printout of Elon Musk's post: Ted Cruz reveals how Trump vs Musk unfolded in front of his eyes, like a 'hand grenade was thrown in the middle of everything'
articles.summary: US News: The major fallout between Donald Trump and Elon Musk last year had a last-minute push from President Trump's closest aide Natalie Harp, Ted Cruz insin.
articles.body: The major fallout between Donald Trump and Elon Musk last year had a last-minute push from President Trump's closest aide Natalie Harp, Ted Cruz insinuated at a recent podcast as he said Natalie just printed Elon Musk's social media post in which he claimed that Trump's name is in the Epstein Files and presented it in front of the president without any filter. Senator Ted Cruz said he was present at the Oval Office when the drama unfolded, when he went to seek the president's support for a school-choice provision.Cruz, a Republican senator from Texas, said he was meeting Trump at the White House in June 2025 to seek the president’s support for a school-choice provision when Musk’s post suddenly derailed the discussion. According to Cruz, Trump’s aide Natalie Harp printed out Musk’s post and handed it directly to the president.Musk had posted on X that it was “time to drop the really big bomb,” alleging that Trump was in the Epstein files and claiming that this was the reason the files had not been made public. Musk later added that the truth would eventually emerge.Cruz described the moment as an extraordinary interruption to what had been a policy discussion.“So what happens when something gets tweeted is [it’s] printed out,” Cruz said in an interview on Patrick Bet-David’s PDB Podcast. “Natalie comes in, printed on a piece of paper and hands it to him. And he literally reads that tweet.”Cruz said he watched Trump’s reaction as he read the post.“I’m sitting in the Oval, and his knuckles turn white,” Cruz recalled, adding that Trump was extremely angry.The senator joked that he learned “some curse words” he had not previously known and said the meeting over school choice effectively ended at that point.Ted Cruz's revelation came at a time when there are a lot of questions on Harp's influence on Trump. Harp has an unusual role as one of the aides who regularly puts information from the internet in front of Trump. She has been dubbed the president’s “human printer” because of her reported practice of printing news stories, social-media posts and other material for him to read.Harp joined Trump’s orbit in 2022 after working as an anchor and host at the conservative One America News Network..Musk had been a prominent ally of Trump and played a major role in the administration’s efforts to reduce federal spending through the Department of Government Efficiency. But their relationship deteriorated publicly in June 2025, with the two men trading increasingly hostile accusations.Musk’s Epstein-related allegation marked a particularly serious escalation. Trump subsequently denied wrongdoing and publicly attacked Musk, while Musk continued his criticism before the feud eventually subsided.Cruz, who said he is also friends with Musk, said he was relieved that the two men eventually repaired their relationship.“It was not good for America to have the two of them battling,” Cruz said, describing the moment he witnessed in the Oval Office as being like “a hand grenade thrown in the middle of everything.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Michigan Democrat who lost Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed takes aim at Bernie Sanders over Israel stance
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens called Bernie Sanders part of an anti-Zionist "sickness" and questioned what he has done for Middle East peace in an interview.
articles.body: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost last month in the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, called out Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., in an interview over his Middle East policy, describing the progressive senator as part of an anti-Zionist "sickness." "I really don’t know what Bernie Sanders has done for peace in the Middle East, for Palestinian dignity; I can’t think of anything he’s totally done. It’s a sickness that needs to end. You know, it’s a linkage towards extremism or jihad, I don’t know," she said in an interview with The Jerusalem Post. Sanders has repeatedly called to end U.S. military aid to Israel and has been outspoken in his criticism of the Israeli government. FORMER BERNIE SANDERS OFFICIAL ACCUSES SENATOR OF PUSHING MOST ANTISEMITIC CANDIDATES 'IN A GENERATION' "I believe that anti-Zionism is a hate movement that has taken over in America and throughout parts of the West," Stevens said in the interview. Sanders' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. "I think that Israel is more than just a punching bag for some of the challenges that America is facing," Stevens said. "There is this bizarre obsession that has reached pitch level with calling out one country, one tiny country in the Middle East." She was critical, however, of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he has been a "problem." BERNIE SANDERS AIMS TO BLOCK SALE OF BOMBS AND BULLDOZERS TO ISRAEL, ACCUSING US ALLY OF 'GENOCIDE' Stevens endorsed El-Sayed shortly after she lost the primary. However, she urged the Democratic Senate candidate to cut ties with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, with whom El-Sayed has campaigned. "It certainly makes sense to get rid of this Hasan Piker affiliation," she said during an interview with Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" in August, also asserting that the Democratic plans for healthcare, democracy and Black-owned businesses are better than those of El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers. Asked whether El-Sayed had said or done anything other than winning the Democratic nomination to earn the support and assuage the concerns of groups that voted for Stevens, such as Jewish voters, Black voters or Reagan-era Democrats, Stevens pointed to her own good performance with those demographics, identifying herself as a Zionist Democrat and asserting that her party had room for all those communities. "I came really close [to winning the primary] and I'm still a Democrat. I'm still out here talking about my views and values. I want the people who share my views and values to feel safe and to feel heard in the Democratic Party," she continued. Qasim Rashid, a SiriusXM radio host and human rights lawyer, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Stevens' comments are "profoundly disappointing and not helpful." "It is a well-established fact that the Israeli government has targeted and killed civilians. Leading human rights organizations and scholars, including Israeli scholars, have documented it as genocide," Rashid said. "Our own Leahy laws in the United States require that we stop funding governments when there is credible evidence of mass human rights atrocities. By continuing to insist on arming Israel as it is violating international human rights law, Haley Stevens is on the wrong side of history. "And she’s also jeopardizing losing the state of Michigan to MAGA Republicans. This is not being thoughtful or logical. It certainly is not following the call of international human rights law and constitutional law that she took a sworn oath to uphold." MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’ Americans' opinions on Israel have soured, according to a poll from March, largely due to Democrats and independents. The results of the survey, by NBC News, come amid sharp political debates among Democrats over support for Israel 2½ years after the start of the war between Israelis and Hamas in Gaza. BERNIE SANDERS DEMANDS DEMOCRATS BAN SUPER PACS FROM PRIMARIES, BLASTS AIPAC, ‘CORRUPT SYSTEM’ Just 32% of Americans view Israel positively, with 39% seeing the Jewish state in a negative light, according to the poll, which was conducted Feb. 27-March 2. That's a sea change from three years ago, when Americans held a positive view of Israel by a 47%-34% margin. articles.title: Frightening scene unfolds on iconic sky ride as child falls down onto boardwalk
articles.summary: A young child fell from Casino Pier's Sky Ride in Seaside Heights, New Jersey, and her aunt then jumped down after her in a frightening boardwalk incident.
articles.body: A frightening scene unfolded on the Jersey Shore this week when a toddler fell from an iconic boardwalk ride and her aunt scrambled to help. The incident took place aboard Casino Pier's Sky Ride, a chairlift-style attraction in Seaside Heights, on Monday, the Asbury Park Press reported. The 2-year-old girl fell at about 7:40 p.m. on the Sky Ride in Seaside Heights before the ride started moving, NJ.com reported. She tumbled to the edge of the boardwalk and sand, according to the outlet. DISNEY SCARE UNFOLDS AFTER TEEN EXITS LOG RIDE MOMENTS BEFORE 50-FOOT PLUNGE A 3-year-old boy who had been riding with the pair remained on the ride — which Casino Pier staff quickly shut down. Firefighters then used a ladder to help the boy descend. The ride is about 10 to 12 feet above the boardwalk, according to the Asbury Park Press. Fire Chief Tim Farrell said the girl fell onto an entrance platform not far below the chair and then onto the sand, according to the newspaper, per Asbury Park Press. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER EMS staff checked the girl soon after she fell. She and her aunt were then transported to the Community Medical Center in Toms River for a medical evaluation, according to reports. Police told the Asbury Park Press the ride appeared to be functioning properly, with no apparent defects. The New Jersey Department of Community Affairs, which oversees amusement ride inspections and licensing, is investigating the incident, according to police. There is no indication at this time of a ride malfunction. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Amusement park database Coasterpedia indicates that the Sky Ride was built by Borvig and opened at Casino Pier in 1983. Fox News Digital reached out to the Seaside Heights Police Department and the Seaside Heights Fire Department for comment. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The Jersey Shore incident is the latest in a string of amusement park ride scares across the country. A woman in Colorado recently suffered serious injuries after she was allegedly ejected from a roller coaster and dragged along the track while still strapped into her seat belt. articles.title: Child sex abuse material on Meta: NHRC notices to IT, I&B ministries
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) as part of the ongoing scrutiny of circulation of child sexual abuse material on Instagram.NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content on a platform. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said.The bench has asked whether a digital platform's legal position can continue to be treated merely as that of a passive intermediary when its systems actively generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish, amplify or monetise content.The commission has specifically asked the I&B ministry whether Meta falls within its regulatory purview as a publisher or publisher of online curated content under IT Rules, 2021 wherever the company's systems generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish or amplify content.Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta and the action required to be taken by the ministry under the existing regulatory framework.The notices to the minis-tries follow ones issued to Delhi Police in July after NHRC took cognisance of allegations concerning paid ads on Instagram that facilitated access to child sexual abuse material. The commission has now sought action taken reports within two weeks from MeitY and the I&B ministry.The matter arose after media reports by BBC World Service alleged that paid advertisements using terms such as "rape video" and "child video" were being displayed on Instagram to redirect users to Telegram channels where such material was allegedly offered for sale.The bench has also sought a response from MeitY regarding compliance with the provision on mandatory reporting of offences under Pocso Act 2012 and on whether the matter was reported to the special juvenile police unit or the local police. If not, MeitY has been asked to identify the officer or authority responsible and indicate the action taken for the lapse.Material placed before NHRC includes screenshots of Meta's systems which, according to the complainant, provide suggestions relating to content ideas, audience engagement strategies and monetisation methods.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
