articles.title: ICE agent charged with lying about shooting Venezuelan man during crackdown
articles.summary: The ICE officer faces federal charges related to the January shooting in Minnesota.
articles.body:
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has been charged with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in the state of Minnesota.

Christian Castro, who was released from custody in Texas last week, faces federal charges relating to shooting on 14 January, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS.

The Department of Homeland Security initially said Castro fired in self-defence after being attacked by three Venezuelan illegal migrants with a shovel and broom handle. Minnesota investigators allege the agent fired through a closed door and shot the man in the leg.

It is rare for the current justice department to accuse a federal agent of breaking the law on the job.

What is ICE and what powers do its agents have to use force?

The federal grand jury in Castro's case returned a six-count indictment against him on Wednesday, reports CBS.

According to US media, officials expect to make the indictment public once Castro is in custody.

The charges against him come after the governor of Texas refused to extradite Castro to Minnesota, where he faces separate charges of assault and false reporting of a crime related to the shooting.

He was arrested in Texas in May and jailed for three months.

Castro was one of thousands of federal immigration officers deployed to Minnesota during Operation Metro Surge, which sparked fierce protests and resulted in the deaths of two US citizens at the hands of agents during confrontations.

Alfredo Alejandro Aljorna and Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, who was shot in the leg and survived, were originally charged with forcibly assaulting, resisting or impeding federal officers.

After surveillance video raised questions about this version of events, federal prosecutors investigated the officers.

In February, ICE said two immigration agents might have made "untruthful statements" about the shooting. They were placed on administrative leave.

The charges against the migrants were dismissed, with prosecutors citing "newly discovered evidence", CBS reported.

Castro was arrested in Texas in May and Minnesota's top prosecutor asked for him to be extradited to stand trial, also filing a lawsuit last month seeking to compel Texas Governor Greg Abbott to sign off on extradition.

Abbott said that he did not approve the request because he had "serious doubts" that Castro qualified as a fugitive.

State officials have said Castro discharged his weapon through the front door of a home "knowing there were people who had just run inside".

The bullet travelled through the door and struck one victim in the leg, making its final impact in the wall of a child's room, they said.

The BBC has approached the office of Minnesota's top prosecutor for comment.

articles.title: SC: BCI writ runs only over lawyers, not law students
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters t.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters threatening to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation.Despite BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra pleading for closure of the issue saying that the objectionable letters to the Hyderabad institute on Aug 13 were withdrawn within hours, a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the ambit of BCI's powers, as the statutory regulatory body for the legal profession, is required to be delineated."From an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that Advocates Act, 1961, whereunder BCI is statutorily created, does not confer any express or implied power on BCI or state bar councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students. BCI has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates," SC said.The bench agreed with senior advocate K Parameshwar who, for former Nalsar law graduate petitioners, argued that BCI does not have jurisdiction over law students, and its Aug 13 letters amounted to making deep inroads into freedom of speech and expression of students.Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SCSo far as law students are concerned, it is the parent institution or the authority prescribed under laws and bylaws governing the institution who alone have the competence to take disciplinary action, if so required, against the students,” said the bench.Parameshwar said while the letter threatened to bar the registration of the Nalsar 2026 batch of law graduates as advocates, a second letter, while withdrawing the threat, directed the university to identify the students who had given the call to oppose the invitation to CJI as chief guest at the convocation. The advocate added that both letters were without jurisdiction.On Aug 14, SC stayed the operation of both letters, terming them “absolutely uncalled for”, and shielded the students and faculty ag-ainst any action by the university pursuant to BCI’s letters.BCI chief Mishra said that both letters were withdrawn subsequently.The CJI-led bench said, “Having held so, we declare all the communications of Aug 13 or subsequent modified communications to be wi-thout any authority of law.”This indictment and clipping of wings of BCI come a day after the same bench entertained petitions alleging serious irregularities in its functioning and its composition without proper elections.On Aug 14, the bench had also said BCI had nothing to do with the students’ protest against the invitation to CJI. “The students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for,” CJI had said.Trashing BCI’s threat, CJI had told Parameshwar to convey to the students “to get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court. We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Dramatic video shows SWAT vehicle ramming tractor during tense Oregon standoff
articles.summary: Oregon man Erik Gordon Shunn allegedly fired more than 200 rounds, shot at a Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office drone and engaged in a standoff with a SWAT team.
articles.body: Video captured the dramatic moment a SWAT team rammed its vehicle into a tractor during a standoff with a suspect who allegedly went on a shooting spree near an Oregon home. Erik Gordon Shunn, 53, reportedly targeted multiple tree workers Saturday afternoon south of Portland before confronting responding authorities, according to the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office (CCSO). Officials said Shunn fired more than 200 rounds throughout the incident. In a video captured by a CCSO drone, Shunn appeared to unleash a barrage of gunfire directly at the aircraft, according to authorities. He was later seen driving a compact tractor near the front of his home when a CCSO SWAT vehicle slammed into it, trapping the tractor against the house. Several SWAT personnel then jumped from the back of the vehicle and moved in to apprehend him. VIDEO SHOWS POLICE TAKE DOWN COP KILLER WITH ARMORED VEHICLE AFTER GUNMAN TURNED NEIGHBORHOOD INTO WAR ZONE According to officials, the Clackamas County SWAT Team responded to a report of an armed neighbor firing at professional arborists hired to cut down trees in a rural residential and farm area. The 911 caller told dispatchers they believed Shunn had several guns, while witnesses estimated he fired roughly 20 rounds at tree company employees, officials said. When the authorities arrived, drones allegedly spotted Shunn in his driveway. LOUISIANA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING DEPUTY US MARSHAL FACES POSSIBLE DEATH PENALTY He was seen "knocking down trees with a tractor in an apparent attempt to create a barricade," according to the CCSO. Authorities said they ultimately decided to pin Shunn’s tractor after he became separated from his rifle while driving it near the front of the home. "SWAT personnel used this window of opportunity because they believed it provided the highest likelihood of safely apprehending Shunn," CCSO officials said. WATCH: MAN ACCUSED OF AIMING FLAMETHROWER AT OFFICERS SERVING EVICTION NOTICE IN WILD BODYCAM VIDEO Shunn was treated at the scene before being taken to a local hospital for evaluation. "First responders also checked on neighbors and tree workers to confirm their safety and evacuate them from the area," CCSO said. No injuries were reported. Shunn’s mother, who was also at the home during the standoff, was also unharmed, according to the sheriff’s office. Shunn was charged with second-degree attempted murder, first-degree attempted assault, recklessly endangering, unlawful use of a weapon, menacing, unlawful possession of firearms, first-degree attempted criminal mischief, and interfering with a peace officer.
